review_kind: Independent, read-only Claude re-review of Academy 2.1 milestone 1 (qualification tooling and fixtures). Not hosted acceptance, not release approval, and not a replacement for the formal independent Codex chunk/phase gate. Milestone 2 hosted execution was not assessed.
required_fixes: RF1 The interactive contracts are chosen by the call's workflow tag, not by the procedure it calls, so a destructive call can avoid them by naming a different workflow. contracts::validate only checks calls whose `workflows` include W53/W65/W66 (contracts.rs:38-46). The failed-precondition block also only applies within the same workflow (live_academy.rs:524-526). `program()` accepts any procedure under any workflow the family may claim (live_academy.rs:242-273). Example: `call.01 W51 progress.resetCourse {"json":{"courseId":"…"}} ?? :object` in L12, or the same under W54 in L13, passes `program()` as long as resetCourse is permitted and the account is designated. It then sends a hard-delete reset with no certificate or progress baseline (Academy progress.ts:262-393 deletes unit, objective, quiz, lab, course-scoped exam and XP rows) and earns W51/W54 credit on a shape check. `exam.start` (spends a real attempt) and `shift.start {daily:true}`/serve/answer/decide (spends the one Daily attempt) can likewise run under W52/W54. That contradicts contracts.rs's own premise ('private manifests choose test data, not whether a boolean shape is enough to prove a destructive reset worked') and the doc's claim that 'a reset cannot run after an earlier failed checkpoint' (follow-up.md:72-74). Fix: tie each contract-governed procedure to its workflow (progress.resetCourse→W66, exam.start→W53, shift.start/serve/answer/decide→W65). Reject any call to those procedures that doesn't claim that workflow, and validate every occurrence, not only the first ordered match (the `iter.find` at contracts.rs:47-53). Add a fixture where a resetCourse tagged W51 is refused and never sent.

RF2 The doc and fixture promise more from the Shift hand-off cleanup than real Academy allows. Real `decideStage` throws BAD_REQUEST 'stage is not complete' whenever an alert is pending (ai-security-academy shift-run.ts:3106-3110), so a hand_off only settles a run that is at a stage boundary. After a failed serve, or a blocked or failed answer mid-stage, the cleanup hand-off will be refused. The spent Daily run then stays active until the stale sweep contains it (shift-run.ts:2011-2017 describes that path). The fixture lets hand_off through after any answer (academy.rs:249-258) and always returns `next:"boundary"`, even after `ungraded`/`breached` (academy.rs:246). The test then calls this 'a designated hand-off can still clean up' (academy.rs:834-841). Correct follow-up.md:73-74 to say hand-off cleanup works only at a stage boundary and that otherwise the Daily attempt is spent and left to the sweep. Record that as the cleanup or reconciliation outcome, and make the fixture refuse a mid-stage hand-off. While editing the doc, also: (a) list ` in ` as a reserved separator next to ` ?? `/` && ` (follow-up.md:47-49). `Expect::parse` splits on ` in ` before `=` (assertions.rs:42), so any equality literal containing ' in ' fails closed. (b) Update the fixture-regression list (follow-up.md:80-84), which predates the wrong attempt/shift ID, ungraded/breached, refused Daily, empty certificate baseline, weak-program and account-binding regressions.
evidence_gaps: G1 I could not recompute any hash. The log sha256 values, the build_inputs hashes for live_academy.rs, assertions.rs, contracts.rs and tests/live_run/academy.rs (run.json:264-266, 290, 464-466, 667-669) and the test-executable hashes were not checked against the files I reviewed. The binding is recorded, not independently verified.

G2 build_inputs lists .rs files and manifests only. It omits compile-time inputs pulled in with include_str!/include_bytes!: crates/desktop-core/assets/case-catalog.json, src/workbench/scm-catalog.json and resources/harness/pin.json. pin.json is dirty from concurrent C26 work. The test-executable hash covers this for the two test records. The clippy record has no equivalent binding. Low impact on Academy logic.

G3 The contracts are conjunctions of many clauses, but the regression test removes only three of them: exam state `:object`, reset-after `:object` and debrief `/themes:array` (academy.rs:852-894). No test shows that each mandatory clause is required on its own. For example: omitting one of the four reset counts or `/cleared/<c>=@before`, a `:array` certificate baseline, missing `=@` on the final certificates, a shift.answer without membership or served-order reference, a decide without the same shiftId, or a serve without the shiftId reference. Dropping any one of these from contracts.rs would not fail the current suite.

G4 Fixture input fidelity is still partial. progress.checkInline, progress.courseSummary, progress.resetCourse and exam.eligibility ignore their inputs (academy.rs:143, 190-214). One test grades with `{unitId, answer}` (academy.rs:561), which real Academy rejects because lessonId and questionId are required (progress.ts:397-402). The courseId consistency the reset relies on is enforced only statically (contracts.rs:144-150). The fixture does not model it.

G5 Real `exam.submissionState` echoes the input attemptId (exam.ts:1453), so `/attemptId=@start/attemptId` cannot fail against Academy. The real protection is the required input reference plus Academy's NOT_FOUND ownership filter. `wrong_exam_identity_fails…` (academy.rs:757-783) tests a server behavior Academy cannot produce. The check is sound, but the strength claimed for it should come from the input reference.

G6 For hosted runs (milestone 2, not run): the W65 contract needs a non-empty debrief (contracts.rs:129-131). Academy returns themes only when some alert has correct=false (shift-narrative.ts:501-512). But `/outcome in ["correct","incorrect"]` also passes an all-correct run, and that run can only fail W65. Nothing yet shows that a deterministic miss can be produced against seeded, hidden alert content. The fixture's stage boundary still comes after a single answer, not after `alertsPerStage` answers (shift-run.ts:199-201). resetCourse deletes course-scoped exam attempts (progress.ts:335-345), which can collide with a W53 attempt on the same course in the same L13 run. `irreversible_exclusions` is still not enforced, and the ledger still reads only the C25 receipt root (both carried from the prior review).
G7 The doc describes a separate read-only live probe (sign-in plus a 50-course catalog read; follow-up.md:131-135), but no receipts for it were in scope. I relied on the doc's description only.
optional_suggestions: S1 Make the per-workflow checkpoint receipt fail, or block, when any call claiming that workflow failed or was blocked. Today, coverage (live_academy.rs:605-628) can be satisfied by a later unvalidated duplicate after the validated call failed. The row is still failed by ledger aggregation (ledger.rs:256-260), but the checkpoint receipt itself reads 'passed'.

S2 Membership receipts write the operator's literal strings (`{"one_of": values}`, assertions.rs:168-171). The doc says private strings record only presence and size (follow-up.md:51-54). Either restrict membership to `/outcome`, or summarize the values the same way Equals does.

S3 Consider requiring `expected_account_sha256` for any family that claims workflow credit, not only families that send mutations. The motivating risk, silent browser approval as an existing account, also lets read-only W50 evidence come from a non-designated or personal learner.

S4 When W65 requires `/themes:nonempty-array`, also require at least one shift.answer that asserts `/outcome="incorrect"`. Or document how a deterministic miss is produced (for example an out-of-range option index), after confirming Academy grades it rather than rejecting it.

S5 Receipts record the designated input template verbatim (live_academy.rs:521-523). For progress.checkInline with `/correct=true` (and shift.answer `values`), this commits an answer key, including lessonId/questionId/answer, to the repo. Consider recording a label in place of the answer value.
S6 The W65 exemption list (contracts.rs:95-101) omits shift.dailyGhost and shift.yesterday. If they take no shiftId, a W65-tagged call to either is rejected. That fails closed, but is surprising.

S7 Carried forward: give `Spec` owned or Cow ids and workflows instead of `Box::leak` (live_academy.rs:290, 366-368, 623), and hard-refuse exam.submit and exam.acknowledgeAward for this qualification.
limitations: Read-only static review. No builds, tests, clippy, endpoint calls or credential access. The private manifest and hosted receipts were not read. Runtime conclusions come from source and the recorded logs: review-remediation-live-run.log shows 48/48 passing, review-remediation-unit.log 18/18 passing, and review-remediation-clippy.log a clean `-D warnings` run (exit 0, run.json:525-529). The older failed clippy record (exit 101) is retained as stated.

Academy contracts were checked against /Users/cdot/development/redtail/ai-security-academy as it stands now: routers shift.ts, exam.ts, progress.ts and certificate.ts, and services shift-run.ts and shift-narrative.ts. The deployed hosted service may differ.

Remediation I confirmed in the current source: unwraps in assertions.rs tests replaced with expect. Exam contract requires `in-progress`, positive `timeLimitSeconds`, a non-empty deadline and attemptId, and an input reference to the started attempt. These match exam.ts:465 and 515-518. W65 shapes match shift-run.ts (ActiveShift.shiftId/alertsAnswered/atBoundary, ServeResult.shift.alertOrder/breachResolved, AnswerResult.outcome with four states, SettleResult.shiftId/status). Settlement must equal the started shiftId. Debrief requires non-empty themes, so the empty unknown-shift payload (shift-narrative.ts:499) cannot pass. Closed membership rejects ungraded/breached. Mutations are blocked after a failure in the same workflow, except a shift.decide hand_off (live_academy.rs:524-538; tested with the empty certificate baseline). The W66 contract requires a non-empty certificate baseline, hasProgress=true, a positive count, all four `/cleared/<c>=@before`, all four counts =0, hasProgress=false, whole-answer certificate equality and the same courseId; these match progress.ts:186-254 and 262-393. Strings, objects and arrays in assertion receipts record only presence and size. Fixtures return 404 for unmodeled procedures and check exam and shift IDs. Account binding comes from `desktop.me` through the core (learner_domain.rs:1422-1460); a mismatch or a malformed hash blocks, stops and signs out before any program or avatar call, and a mutation without a designated hash is refused at parse time. `observe` cannot be used for mutations and earns no workflow credit. Every case in the prior review's G3 and G5 now has a regression.
The unsalted `account_sha256` in sign-in receipts remains. It is acceptable only because the account IDs accepted (UUIDs or Clerk `user_…`, academy.rs:176-181) are high-entropy.
Concurrent dirty C26/UI files outside the named scope were not reviewed.
recommendation: minor revise. The previous review's RF1-RF8 and both of its blockers are substantially resolved, the identity binding is sound, and the validation records are now bound to their build inputs and pass. One real gap remains: contracts apply by workflow tag rather than by procedure, so a destructive reset, exam start or Daily start can be dispatched under a different workflow with weak assertions (RF1). The hand-off cleanup and fixture also overstate what real Academy allows (RF2). Fix both, add the per-clause contract regressions if practical (G3), then take it to the formal Codex gate. Nothing here constitutes hosted qualification.
